title: Inclined planes
examples: How do I find the component of weight parallel to the slope?
What is the difference between weight and the normal force on a ramp?
If the slope is rough, how does friction affect the calculation?

explain.say: Today we explore forces acting on an inclined plane.
First we must resolve the weight vector into components.

draw.text: Weight Components: W sin θ, W cos θ

explain.say: The component parallel to the slope causes the slide down.

draw.text: Force down slope: W sin θ

explain.say: Next we look at the normal reaction force.

draw.text: Normal Force: N = W cos θ

explain.say: In the absence of other forces, the normal reaction balances the perpendicular weight component.
For a real-life example consider sliding a box down a ramp.

faq.q: What is the angle theta in these calculations?
faq.a: Theta is the angle the inclined plane makes with the horizontal ground.
asks: What is the angle of inclination?
How do I find the slope angle?

faq.q: Does the normal force change if the surface is rough?
faq.a: No, the normal force only depends on the perpendicular component of weight, not friction.
asks: Is N related to the friction force?

faq.q: If the slope is vertical, what happens to the forces?
faq.a: If the slope is vertical, the parallel component becomes the full weight, and the normal force is horizontal.
asks: What if the angle is ninety degrees?
How does the math change for a wall?

faq.q: Do I need to use the angle of the slope or the angle of the weight?
faq.a: You must use the angle the slope makes with the horizontal, which is theta.
asks: Which angle do I use for sin and cos?
Is it the angle of the ramp or the weight?

faq.q: What if the object is accelerating up the slope?
faq.a: If accelerating up, you must include the net force causing the upward acceleration in your equations.
asks: How do I calculate upward acceleration?
What if I am pulling it up?

facts: The weight vector (W) is always perpendicular to the ground.
The component of weight parallel to the slope is W times the sine of the angle theta.
The normal reaction force (N) always acts perpendicular to the surface.
The sum of the perpendicular components of forces must be zero.

quiz.say: A block rests on a slope making an angle of thirty degrees. What is the normal force?
quiz.why: The normal force balances the perpendicular component of weight, which is W cos theta.

wrong.1: This incorrectly uses the sine component, which is parallel to the slope.
wrong.2: This assumes the slope is horizontal, ignoring the angle theta.
wrong.3: This incorrectly assumes no normal force exists on the surface.

quiz.say: If the parallel component of weight is calculated as W sin θ, what does this represent?
quiz.show: Force parallel to slope: W sin θ

options.show: The force pulling the object down the slope.
options.say: The force pulling the object down the slope.

options.show: The total weight of the object.
options.say: The total weight of the object.

options.show: The force perpendicular to the slope.
options.say: The force perpendicular to the slope.

quiz.why: This component is responsible for the motion down the inclined plane.

wrong.0: The normal force is equal to the perpendicular component, not the parallel one.
wrong.2: The total weight is the hypotenuse, not just the parallel part.
wrong.3: The perpendicular force uses the cosine function, not the sine function.

quiz.say: If the slope angle theta is ninety degrees, the normal force acts:
quiz.why: When the slope is vertical, the normal force acts purely horizontally, balancing the horizontal component of weight.

wrong.0: The normal force is always perpendicular to the surface, regardless of the slope angle.
wrong.2: The normal force always acts perpendicular to the surface it rests on.
wrong.3: A vertical surface provides a normal force unless the object is weightless.
